001package io.jstach.rainbowgum.annotation;
002
003import static java.lang.annotation.ElementType.FIELD;
004import static java.lang.annotation.RetentionPolicy.SOURCE;
005
006import java.lang.annotation.Documented;
007import java.lang.annotation.Retention;
008import java.lang.annotation.Target;
009
010/**
011 * API documentation marker on an enum constant listing the other property values, case
012 * insensitive, that select it besides its own name, for example <code>true</code> or
013 * <code>false</code>.
014 * <p>
015 * Property enums follow the same conventions so that users can guess values without
016 * looking them up:
017 * <ul>
018 * <li><code>true</code> turns the thing on or shows it, usually in its default form; when
019 * the default is off, <code>true</code> selects the usual on choice instead (caller info:
020 * <code>basic</code>).</li>
021 * <li><code>false</code> turns the thing off or hides it, selecting the constant named
022 * <code>OFF</code> or <code>NONE</code>.</li>
023 * <li><code>default</code> restores the default without naming it, so a later property
024 * source can undo an earlier one; it differs from <code>true</code> only when the default
025 * is off. When a constant is itself named <code>DEFAULT</code>, it is not aliased.</li>
026 * <li>A constant named <code>OFF</code> is for a switch or mode that is turned off
027 * (color, strict checking, debug output); a constant named <code>NONE</code> is for a
028 * part or piece of content that is left out (no timestamp, no key values, no caller
029 * info).</li>
030 * <li>An alias never repeats a constant's own name; names already match case
031 * insensitively.</li>
032 * </ul>
033 *
034 * @apiNote Rainbow Gum's annotation processor records these aliases in generated resource
035 * files for its own tests. Those files are not public API: their names, location, and
036 * format may change in any release and must not be relied on.
037 */
038@Documented
039@Retention(SOURCE)
040@Target(FIELD)
041public @interface EnumAlias {
042
043        /**
044         * The aliases.
045         * @return aliases.
046         */
047        String[] value();
048
049}
